evidence_note: Pocket: Stewards/Helm pair; Archive sole negative. Absolutist Denmark-Norway (Christian VII/Struensee): Stewards (landed aristocracy dominant) + Helm (crown direction — Struensee's executive reforms 1770-72, then reaction under Guldberg). Archive negative = administrative disruption: Struensee's rapid reform programme dismantled continuity of record-keeping; after his execution 1772 the bureaucracy was rebuilt by Guldberg, leaving Archive as the unstable trailing node throughout the era. Official: confident absolutist-reformist monarchy. Popular: gentry-dominated society. Sources confirm the Struensee-era institutional volatility making Archive the damaged node.

Pocket: Craft/Stewards pair (Hands/Helm/Shield positive); all positive, Archive marginal. Great Agrarian Reform era under Crown Prince Frederik's regency (Bernstorff): Craft (productive technique — agricultural reform improving yields); Stewards (landlord-peasant restructuring, freeholder class emerging); Hands (newly freed peasants acquiring property and agency); Helm (reformist regency government); Shield (Dano-Norwegian military). Archive marginal = administrative reconstruction ongoing after the Struensee disruption. Popular: cautious optimism for peasant-freeholder class. Official: reformist confidence. The all-positive Craft/Stewards-led agrarian-reform topology closely matches the period.

Pocket: Craft/Stewards pair (Hands/Helm/Shield positive); all positive, Archive marginal — identical text to era II. The all-positive topology describes Denmark-Norway's productive and administrative functioning, but the pocket does not capture the British bombardment of Copenhagen (1807) and forced adherence to Napoleon's Continental System. Official: nationalist anger at British attack, alliance with France. Institutional: functioning under wartime conditions. Popular: partial — anti-British sentiment, but British naval blockade created real economic hardship not captured by all-positive. The identical pocket to era II means this topology cannot distinguish the wartime shock from the reform era. Broad because the British bombardment and economic disruption of the Continental System constitute a meaningful absence from the all-positive description.

Pocket: Craft/Stewards pair (Hands/Helm/Shield positive); all positive, Archive marginal — identical text to eras II-III. The loss of Norway to Sweden at the Treaty of Kiel (1814) is the defining event of this era — a catastrophic territorial contraction. All-positive topology for a 25-year era that opens with Denmark ceding Norway (the other half of the kingdom) is a meaningful tension. Official: adjusted to reduced territory, rebuilt around Danish core. Institutional: post-1814 reconstruction proceeded, and Craft/Stewards-led internal development is real (Copenhagen trade). Popular: partial — post-1814 mood combined grief at Norway's loss with resignation and gradual recovery orientation; the identical pocket to the reform-era does not capture the territorial loss event. Broad because the loss of Norway creates a register gap, even if the subsequent recovery orientation (Craft/Stewards) is correctly captured.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Stewards/Helm/Flow positive); all positive, Archive marginal. 1848 democratic revolution in Denmark and First Schleswig War: Craft/Hands leading (agricultural and labour activation in a period of democratic awakening — peasant and artisan class demanding constitutional rights). 1848: peaceful constitutional revolution in Copenhagen, Frederick VII granted a constitution; First Schleswig war begins. Helm positive = new constitutional government. Flow positive = commerce continuing. Archive marginal = old administrative order being replaced by constitutional institutions. Popular: 1848 democratic mobilisation. Official: constitutional transition. Close match for Craft/Hands-led democratic awakening topology.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Stewards/Helm/Flow positive); all positive, Archive marginal — identical to era V. Post-First-Schleswig-War constitutional government. Recovery 1850-63: rising agricultural and industrial prosperity; National Liberal governments; rising nationalism building toward Second Schleswig war. Craft/Hands + Stewards/Helm/Flow positive topology matches the constitutional prosperity era. Archive marginal = constitutional system still being consolidated. Popular: moderate nationalism. Official: National Liberal confidence. Close match even under identical pocket constraint.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Stewards/Helm/Flow positive); all positive, Archive marginal — identical to eras V-VI. The 1864 defeat to Prussia and Austria (Second Schleswig War) and loss of Schleswig-Holstein is the defining national trauma of modern Danish history. All-positive topology for an era opened by catastrophic territorial defeat cannot capture the initial emotional register. Popular: disagree — the defeat was deeply traumatising; national mourning and humiliation dominated 1864-66. Official: partial — the post-defeat government (Estrup era beginning) pivoted to 'what is lost outwardly shall be regained inwardly' (Dalgas/Hedeselskabet), which is Craft/Hands-led internal recovery — the topology captures the recovery orientation but not the defeat's emotional register. Institutional: partial for same reason. Partial overall because the defeat substantially changes the emotional register even if Craft/Hands led the recovery.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Stewards/Helm/Flow positive); all positive, Archive marginal — identical to eras V-VII. Post-defeat era: agricultural cooperative movement (Andelsbevægelsen) and rising labour movement. Craft/Hands leading is an excellent fit — the cooperative movement was the DEFINING feature of Danish social life 1870-1900 (dairy cooperatives, cooperative slaughterhouses, peasant class gaining power). Helm positive with Stewards positive is the structural tension: Estrup's provisional-law regime (1877-94) represented a Helm that was deeply contested — Estrup governed by provisional finance laws against the parliamentary Left for 17 years, which is not a 'positive-sigma Helm' in terms of democratic coherence. Official: partial because Helm-positive does not capture Estrup's contested-legitimacy governance. Popular: Craft/Hands-led cooperative movement broadly agrees. Institutional: Archive marginal fits (cooperative institutions were extra-parliamentary). Broad overall because Helm-positive in Estrup's provisional-law era is a meaningful tension with official and institutional registers.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Helm/Archive/Flow positive); Lore marginal. WWI neutral Denmark (eras X-XII share identical pocket text — Craft/Hands leaders, Lore marginal, all positive). WWI neutrality and war-trade prosperity: Craft (industry, particularly shipping and food exports); Hands (labour, wartime full employment); Helm (government managing neutral interests); Archive (institutional record-keeping); Flow (war-trade profits). Lore marginal = cultural life somewhat suppressed by wartime caution; no major cultural movement this era. Popular: economic gains mixed with wartime anxiety. Official: neutral-pragmatist confidence. Close match.

evidence_note: Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Helm/Archive/Flow positive); Lore marginal — identical to era X. Post-war era: Northern Schleswig returned to Denmark via 1920 plebiscite (reunification — a hugely positive national moment); then economic turbulence of 1920s, Social Democrats rising. Craft/Hands + Helm/Archive/Flow positive topology matches the period: industrial and labour activation (DNA growing); institutional continuity. Lore marginal — moderate cultural life, no defining cultural event. The 1920 Schleswig reunion is a joyful national event that fits a broadly positive topology. 1929-32 depression beginning but partially insulated by agricultural exports. Close match.

Pocket: Craft/Hands pair (Helm/Archive/Flow positive); Lore marginal — identical to eras X-XI. Social Democratic Stauning government and Kanslergade Agreement 1933. The 1933 Kanslergade Agreement was a historic labour-capital compact (Social Democrats + trade unions + agricultural interests) that resolved the Depression crisis and laid foundations for the Danish welfare state. Craft/Hands leading is the best-fit pocket in this identical group: the Agreement was explicitly a Craft/Hands mobilisation (industrial labour + agricultural labour). Helm positive = Stauning government's executive leadership. Flow positive = economic stabilisation. Lore marginal = Social Democratic ideology present but not culturally dominant. This is the strongest match among the three identical eras.

Pocket: Lore leads (Archive/Helm/Craft positive); Shield negative. German occupation 1940-45: Lore leading (resistance narrative — BBC Danish broadcasts, Freedom Council, rescue of Jews to Sweden 1943, national cultural identity sustaining occupation) + Archive (institutional record-keeping, government continued until Aug 1943 then resistance-government) + Helm + Craft (economic production under occupation). Shield negative = no independent Danish military after April 9 1940 surrender; armed forces disbanded. This is a distinctive, non-identical pocket and exactly describes the occupation topology: narrative-resistance (Lore) dominant over disabled military (Shield negative). Official: institutional-cooperation then resistance. Popular: majority passive resistance, active rescue of Jews. Close match.

sources.title: Rescue of the Danish Jews – Wikipedia

evidence_note: Pocket: Archive leads (Lore/Craft/Hands positive); Shield marginal. Post-liberation reconstruction: Archive (Marshall Plan administration, welfare-state legislation — National Health Act 1973 precursors, social insurance expansion); Lore (liberation and resistance narrative continuing); Craft (reconstruction production); Hands (full employment). Shield marginal = NATO membership 1949, peacetime but Cold War building. Popular: post-liberation national pride and reconstruction optimism. Official: Social Democratic welfare-state construction confidence. Sources confirm Archive-led post-war reconstruction topology.

Pocket: Shield/Archive pair (Helm/Lore/Craft positive); Stewards marginal. Long Social Democratic era: Archive (welfare-state construction) + Shield (Cold War NATO defence commitment — Denmark did maintain conscript army and met NATO targets during this era) + Helm + Lore + Craft. Stewards marginal = capital class politically subordinated to Social Democratic management. Shield is institutionally defensible (Denmark ran a substantial conscript military, Korean War 1950-53 participation, Berlin crisis preparations), but popular register does not identify Shield as a defining leading force — the welfare state (Archive/Lore) is the era's self-understanding. Broad because the Shield/Archive pairing, while institutionally accurate, does not match how popular mood experienced the era's dominant activation (welfare-state rather than military).

Pocket: Craft leads (Hands/Flow/Stewards positive); Shield marginal. EEC membership 1972 and economic turbulence: Craft (manufacturing and industrial development within EEC) + Hands (labour — 1973 Maastricht/Folketing negotiations, Schlüter government from 1982) + Flow (EEC trade expansion) + Stewards (capital under EEC integration). Shield marginal = NATO peacetime. 1972 EEC referendum accepted (63.6% Yes), indicating broad popular consent to Flow-activation. Oil crises 1973, 1979 created hardship but Danish economy adapted. Popular: EEC as Craft/Flow-activating. Official: confident EEC integration and eventual Schlüter economic reform. Close match.

evidence_note: Pocket: Craft leads (Hands/Flow/Stewards positive); Shield marginal — identical to era XVI. Post-Cold War era: 1992 Maastricht rejection (50.7% No) then Edinburgh Agreement acceptance 1993; Social Democratic Nyrup Rasmussen government. Craft/Hands + Flow/Stewards positive topology matches continued EEC/EU integration prosperity. 1992 Maastricht rejection is a significant national sovereignty assertion (Lore-flavoured) but Lore is not in the pocket's positive group, suggesting the economic-functional (Craft/Hands/Flow) register dominates. Shield marginal = post-Cold War drawdown. Popular: prosperity and EEC ambivalence. Official: Copenhagen criteria, EU enlargement engagement. Close match.

Pocket: Craft/Archive pair (Flow/Stewards/Helm positive); Lore marginal. VK centre-right government (Fogh Rasmussen, Løkke Rasmussen): Craft (manufacturing, flexicurity model) + Archive (institutional governance) + Flow + Stewards + Helm. Lore marginal is the significant tension: the 2005 Jyllands-Posten Mohammed cartoon publication triggered a global controversy that was one of the most intense public-discourse events in modern Danish history (diplomatic crisis, fatwa, embassy protests). Lore-marginal topology for an era defined by an international Lore event (freedom of press vs religious sensibility, national identity debate) is a meaningful register gap. Popular: partial — the cartoon controversy divided public opinion sharply. Official: Fogh Rasmussen defended press freedom robustly. Institutional: Lore-marginal does not capture the centrality of the debate. Broad.

Pocket: Craft/Archive pair (Flow/Stewards/Helm positive); Lore marginal — identical to era XVIII. Thorning-Schmidt then Løkke Rasmussen governments: 2015 European refugee crisis was the defining political event (Denmark enacted the most restrictive immigration laws in EU, 'jewellery law' Jan 2016). Lore-marginal topology for an era defined by intense public narrative contestation around immigration, national identity, and welfare-state solidarity is a meaningful tension. Popular: partial — refugee debate deeply divided public (Lore contested). Official: aggressively anti-immigration rhetorical posture (Lore-active). Institutional: agree (Craft/Archive/Flow correctly captures Danish flexicurity model continuing). Broad because Lore-marginal does not capture the politically dominant narrative contestation of the refugee crisis era.

evidence_note: Pocket: Craft/Archive pair (Flow/Stewards/Helm positive); Lore marginal — identical to eras XVIII-XIX. Mette Frederiksen Social Democratic government: COVID pandemic management (Archive dominant — OECD-praised health management); Craft (Danish industrial production continuing); Flow (trade); Stewards (fiscal relief packages); Helm (Frederiksen's executive authority — high approval ratings). Lore marginal = public-discourse events (mink slaughter Nov 2020 controversy, parliamentary dissolution, Ukraine support debates) are present but not topology-dominant. Popular: Frederiksen's pandemic management broadly popular. Official: confident Social Democratic governance. Sources confirm Archive/Craft-led institutional management topology with Helm active.
